title: Gradient-clip threshold hardcoded to 1.0, ignores cfg.max_grad_norm; did_clip logging uses the config value
description: make_optimizer always clips at the module constant _CLIP_NORM=1.0 and never reads cfg.max_grad_norm. The default cfg.max_grad_norm is also 1.0 so the two agree by coincidence, but any run that sets max_grad_norm to something other than 1.0 will silently still clip at 1.0. Worse, the clip-trigger logging in scripts/train_jax.py:471 compares the emitted pre-clip grad norm against cfg.max_grad_norm (extra['did_clip'] = bool(chunk_gnorms_np[i] > cfg.max_grad_norm)), so with a non-default config the logged did_clip flag is computed against a threshold the optimizer never actually used. The config field becomes a no-op knob that also corrupts the clip-trigger metric.
evidence: _CLIP_NORM: Final[float] = 1.0 ... return optax.chain(_branchless_clip_by_global_norm(_CLIP_NORM), inner)  — no reference to cfg.max_grad_norm anywhere in trainer.py (grep for max_grad_norm in trainer.py returns nothing). run_config.py:112 defines `max_grad_norm: float = 1.0`. train_jax.py:471: `extra["did_clip"] = bool(chunk_gnorms_np[i] > cfg.max_grad_norm)`.
suggestion: Pass cfg.max_grad_norm into make_optimizer and use it as the clip threshold: `_branchless_clip_by_global_norm(cfg.max_grad_norm)`. Then the did_clip comparison in train_jax.py is consistent with the actual clip. Alternatively remove cfg.max_grad_norm if 1.0 is truly fixed, but the field is presented as configurable.
verify_note: Verified directly. trainer.py:617 `return optax.chain(_branchless_clip_by_global_norm(_CLIP_NORM), inner)` with `_CLIP_NORM: Final[float] = 1.0` (line 69). A repo-wide grep for max_grad_norm in trainer.py returns NOTHING — make_optimizer never reads cfg.max_grad_norm. run_config.py:112 defines `max_grad_norm: float = 1.0` as a configurable field. train_jax.py:471 `extra["did_clip"] = bool(chunk_gnorms_np[i] > cfg.max_grad_norm)` compares against the config value. The branchless clip triggers (rescales) when g_norm > _CLIP_NORM strictly, and did_clip uses `>` against cfg.max_grad_norm — these agree only because both default to 1.0. Any config setting max_grad_norm != 1.0 silently still clips at 1.0 AND mis-computes did_clip against an unused threshold. The field is a no-op knob and the metric is corrupted under non-default config. High is appropriate: silent miscalibration of a documented training knob plus a corrupted observability metric, no crash to surface it.

title: prepend_outcome is silently ignored by the supernet pretrainer
description: prepend_outcome is a BaseRunConfig flag documented (here and in CLAUDE.md) as the gate that ALL FIVE S8 generation diagnostics condition on. The Lichess data path threads it through (pawn/lichess_data.py:370,414), but the supernet pretrainer never reads cfg.prepend_outcome: scripts/train_jax.py calls generate_corpus(n_games=..., max_ply=cfg.seq_len, seq_len=cfg.seq_len, seed=seed) with no prepend_outcome argument, so it always takes the default False. There is also no --prepend-outcome CLI flag in train_jax.py. A user who sets prepend_outcome=True (accepted by pydantic) to pretrain an outcome-conditioned supernet gets an outcome-UNconditioned model with no error. The three published variants sliced from that supernet then permanently fail every generation diagnostic.
evidence: run_config.py:120-123 documents prepend_outcome as gating the diagnostics; scripts/train_jax.py:337-338 `corpus = generate_corpus(n_games=n_games, max_ply=cfg.seq_len, seq_len=cfg.seq_len, seed=seed,)` omits prepend_outcome; `grep -n prepend scripts/train_jax.py` returns nothing.
suggestion: Thread cfg.prepend_outcome into generate_corpus(...) in train_jax.py (both the on-the-fly random-game build and any val build), add the --prepend-outcome CLI flag, or — if outcome-conditioned pretraining is genuinely unsupported — reject prepend_outcome=True in PretrainConfig with a clear ValueError instead of silently dropping it.
verify_note: Confirmed and actually UNDERSTATED. generate_corpus DOES accept prepend_outcome (corpus.py:309, keyword-only, default False), but scripts/train_jax.py:336-338 omits it, so pretraining always packs prepend_outcome=False. There is no --prepend-outcome CLI flag in either training script (grep for 'prepend' add_argument returns nothing). pydantic accepts prepend_outcome=True on BaseRunConfig with no error. The finder claimed the adapter/Lichess path 'threads it through' — that is wrong at the call site: scripts/train_jax_adapter.py:451-466 calls load_lichess_corpus and :442-448 calls generate_corpus WITHOUT passing cfg.prepend_outcome. So the flag is inert across BOTH v2 training entry points, not just pretrain. The library functions (lichess_data.py:370,414; corpus.py:309) have the param but no production caller passes it. A user setting prepend_outcome=True silently trains an outcome-unconditioned model, and all five S8 generation diagnostics (which gate on it) will permanently report _skipped/fail on the published slices. High severity stands; scope is broader than the finding states.

title: apply_film does not implement FiLM — folds gamma/beta into RMSNorm weights instead of an affine on the hidden stream
description: FiLM is defined (Perez et al., and v1 git show main:pawn/adapters/film.py) as h_adapted = gamma ⊙ h_l + beta_l applied to the post-block residual stream, and logits_adapted = gamma_out ⊙ logits + beta_out on the OUTPUT LOGITS (gamma_out/beta_out shape = vocab_size). v2 instead does new_ffn_norm_w = ffn_norm_w * gamma and new_attn_norm_w = attn_norm_w + beta. (1) gamma scales the *normalized FFN sublayer input*, not the layer output stream. (2) beta is ADDED to attn_norm_w; since RMSNorm output = normed * weight, this is a per-channel MULTIPLICATIVE scale of the normalized attention input (factor 1 + beta/w), not the additive residual-stream shift FiLM requires. (3) output_gamma/output_beta are shape (d_model,) folded into final_norm_w, so the 'output FiLM' scales/shifts the final-norm weight rather than the logits, on the wrong axis and wrong tensor. None of the three operations is FiLM. The docstring itself admits the model has no bias term and then mislabels the workaround 'FiLM-equivalent'. Hybrid inherits this via apply_film(apply_lora(...)). Tests only check identity-at-init and shapes (test_jax_adapters.py:638-686), never the trained math, and even assert output_gamma.shape==(d_model,) as 'v1 parity' though v1 used vocab_size — so the regression is uncaught.
evidence: new_ffn_norm_w = layers.ffn_norm_w * adapter.gamma ... new_attn_norm_w = layers.attn_norm_w + adapter.beta  # v2; vs v1: 'h_adapted = γ_l ⊙ h_l + β_l (hidden layers); logits_adapted = γ_out ⊙ logits + β_out (output)' with FiLMLayer(cfg.vocab_size) for output.
suggestion: Implement true FiLM via the existing attn_hook/ffn_hook injection mechanism (like bottleneck): apply h = gamma_l * h + beta_l on the post-layer residual stream, and apply output gamma/beta to the logits with shape vocab_size (requires a logits-side hook or a thin wrapper module rather than folding into norm weights). Add a numeric test that compares against an explicit reference gamma⊙h+beta with non-trivial gamma/beta, not just identity-at-init.
verify_note: Re-read pawn/adapters/film.py:71-128 and pawn/model.py:704-812 (forward) plus v1 (git show main:pawn/adapters/film.py). The model is PRE-NORM: attn_norm_w/ffn_norm_w are RMSNorm weights applied to the *input* of each sublayer (normed = _rmsnorm(h, layer.attn_norm_w)), not the post-block residual stream. (1) new_ffn_norm_w = ffn_norm_w * gamma scales the normalized FFN-sublayer INPUT, not the layer output. (2) new_attn_norm_w = attn_norm_w + beta: since RMSNorm out = normed * weight, adding beta to the weight yields normed * (w+beta) = a per-channel MULTIPLICATIVE rescale (factor 1+beta/w) of the normalized attention input, NOT the additive residual-stream shift FiLM defines (h = gamma*h+beta). The code comment itself calls this 'FiLM-equivalent' which is mathematically false. (3) output_gamma/output_beta fold into final_norm_w (d_model) instead of modulating logits at vocab_size. v1 explicitly implemented h_adapted = gamma*h_l + beta_l on the post-block stream and logits_adapted = gamma_out*logits + beta_out via FiLMLayer(cfg.vocab_size). So v2 is not FiLM in any of the three operations. Tests (test_jax_adapters.py:638-697) only assert identity-at-init and shapes; test_film_identity_at_init... checks bare==filmed at init (gamma=1,beta=0) but never exercises trained non-trivial gamma/beta against a gamma*h+beta reference, so the semantic divergence is uncaught. The model DOES expose attn_hook/ffn_hook post-residual injection points (used by bottleneck) that a true FiLM could use, so the correct mechanism was available. Downgraded critical->high: it is a genuine semantic regression and the adapter learns a different (and weaker, since the beta 'shift' is actually a constrained reparameterization tied to existing norm weights) function space than the documented FiLM; but it is not a crash/data-corruption critical, the forward is still differentiable and trainable, and hybrid only inherits the same reparameterization. The capability loss (no real per-channel additive stream shift, no logit-space output FiLM) is the substance.

title: Adapter training loop dispatches one eqx.filter_jit step per iteration instead of a K-step lax.scan, losing the host-overhead amortization the pretrain path was designed around
description: The pretrain trainer (pawn/trainer.make_scan_step, used by scripts/train_jax.py:291) wraps K inner steps in one jax.lax.scan so per-step host work (RNG, batch gather, Python dispatch, device launch) is amortized. The adapter trainer instead runs a plain Python for-loop calling the single-step closure (step_fn(state, batch)) per iteration, paying full per-step host cost: rng.integers + slice_batch (host numpy gather + jnp.asarray H2D transfer) + a separate donate='all' jit launch every step. adapter_trainer.make_adapter_scan_step exists and is exactly the K-step lax.scan wrapper for this case, but it is dead code (only referenced by tests, never by the training script). For cheap adapters (LoRA rank 4, FiLM) the per-step backbone-frozen compute is small, so host overhead dominates — this is a real throughput regression relative to the subsystem's own pretrain design.
evidence: for offset in range(n_steps): ... batch = slice_batch(corpus, idx); state, loss = step_fn(state, batch)  # one jit dispatch per step. make_adapter_scan_step defined at adapter_trainer.py:305 but grep shows zero non-test callers.
suggestion: Drive the adapter loop through make_adapter_scan_step with a K-chunk of pre-gathered batches (leading K axis), mirroring make_scan_step in the pretrain path; flush metrics between chunks. Keep the single-step path only for eval.
verify_note: Re-read scripts/train_jax_adapter.py:548-585 (_run_steps): a plain Python `for offset in range(n_steps)` calling step_fn(state, batch) once per iteration, where step_fn is make_adapter_train_step's eqx.filter_jit(donate='all') single-step closure (adapter_trainer.py:261-302). Each iteration also runs host-side rng.integers + slice_batch, and slice_batch (trainer.py:93-102) does per-field numpy gather + jnp.asarray H2D transfer EVERY step ('Performs the host -> device transfer at the boundary'). make_adapter_scan_step (adapter_trainer.py:305-331) is exactly the K-step lax.scan(donate='all') wrapper for this case, but grep across the repo shows zero production callers (only adapter_trainer.py def/docstring/__all__, tests, and test_public_api). Meanwhile the pretrain path drives make_scan_step (trainer.py) from scripts/train_jax.py:291 with the explicit rationale 'Whole training loop as one compiled program -- eliminate per-step launch and dispatch overhead.' So the subsystem ships a dead K-step scan wrapper and the script pays full per-step host overhead, a real throughput regression relative to the pretrain design, most impactful for cheap adapters (LoRA r4 / FiLM) where backbone-frozen device compute is small. High is appropriate (efficiency, not correctness; severity tempered only because it doesn't affect results).

title: Weight-folded adapter resume re-inits adapter to identity but warm-starts Adam moments from the previous (non-identity) trajectory
description: On --resume, only bottleneck adapters reload their sidecar weights; every weight-folded strategy (lora/film/sparse/hybrid/unfreeze) keeps the freshly init'd identity adapter (B=0, delta=0, gamma=1, beta=0) while loading optimizer.safetensors via unflatten_opt_state. Two issues: (1) The previously-trained delta was folded irreversibly into the saved backbone, so resume trains a NEW delta from zero on top of the folded weights — for LoRA the effective correction is now an old full-rank baked perturbation plus a new rank-r delta, a silent change in the adaptation structure across the resume boundary. (2) The warm-started Adam mu/nu were accumulated against the previous adapter's gradients, but the adapter params are reset to identity init; bias-corrected moments are then applied to parameters they don't correspond to, corrupting the first updates after resume. Only RoSA+resume is rejected (line 319-321); weight-folded resume is allowed and the docstring openly calls this 'cold-start the adapter PyTree but warm-start the optimizer state'.
evidence: if sidecar.is_file() and isinstance(strategy_cfg, BottleneckConfig): adapter = load_bottleneck_adapter(...)  # only bottleneck reloads; else opt_state = unflatten_opt_state(opt_state, flat) with adapter still at init.
suggestion: Either persist + reload the adapter PyTree for all strategies (a sidecar like bottleneck's), or cold-start the optimizer state when the adapter is cold-started (fresh opt_state) so the moments match the params. A warm optimizer with a cold params PyTree is never correct.
verify_note: Re-read scripts/train_jax_adapter.py:377-416 + _save:477-534. On --resume: backbone=load_model(ckpt_dir) loads the EFFECTIVE folded model (_save writes apply_fn(backbone,adapter), not the raw backbone); only BottleneckConfig reloads its sidecar (line 393-394); all weight-folded strategies (lora/film/sparse/hybrid/unfreeze) keep the freshly init'd identity adapter from line 357; opt_state is warm-loaded via unflatten_opt_state from optimizer.safetensors (399-403). Claim (2) is the real bug: Adam mu/nu accumulated against the PREVIOUS adapter's gradients are applied (bias-corrected) to params that were reset to identity init (LoRA B=0, sparse delta=0, FiLM gamma=1/beta=0) -- the first updates after resume use stale moments incoherent with the cold params. Claim (1) is also real but more nuanced/less severe: the previous delta is folded irreversibly into the saved backbone and a fresh delta trains on top, so the adaptation structure changes across the boundary (multiple stacked low-rank deltas span higher effective rank); arguably more expressive rather than strictly wrong. NUANCE I verified: for `unfreeze`, init_unfreeze_adapter (unfreeze.py:76-100) re-clones the (now-trained, folded) backbone layers, so the adapter resumes at the trained values and the warm moments are roughly coherent -- unfreeze is largely fine; the warm-opt/cold-param mismatch genuinely bites only the 4 delta-based strategies. v1 (git show main:pawn/adapters/rosa.py:320-345) had explicit state_dict/load_adapter_state_dict persisting the adapter params, so this is also a v1 capability the v2 weight-folded path silently dropped. Confirmed high: real first-step-after-resume corruption for 4 of 5 weight-folded strategies, with a clean fix (cold-start opt_state when cold-starting the adapter, or persist+reload the adapter PyTree like bottleneck).

title: Documented carve-from-train val split is unimplemented; train and val read identical rows (100% leak)
description: The module docstring and CLAUDE.md advertise `--pgn-val-split ""` as a carve-from-train mode for single-file/local datasets without a held-out split. No code anywhere partitions rows between train and val. `_scan_parquet` for a local dir globs `<split>-*.parquet` and, when absent, falls back to ALL `*.parquet` for BOTH split="train" and split="validation". So for any single-file local source the train load and the val load scan the exact same files and (with the same filters) produce the same games. The adapter trainer then samples val batches from this identical pool, making val loss a pure train-loss echo. The CLAUDE.md leak warning ("Carving val out of train silently leaks") describes a behavior the code does not actually guard against or implement.
evidence: candidates = sorted(path.glob(f"{split}-*.parquet")); if not candidates: candidates = sorted(path.glob("*.parquet")) — same fallback for split='train' and split='validation'. No row-level split/holdout exists; `git grep` for holdout/carve/partition in lichess_data.py returns only the docstring at line 131.
suggestion: Either implement an actual deterministic row-level carve (e.g. hash-of-game-id or seeded shuffle + index split, with the split fraction + seed baked into the cache key) when split-prefixed shards are absent, or remove the carve-from-train claim and hard-error when a `validation` split is requested but only undifferentiated `*.parquet` exists, so the user can't silently train==val.
verify_note: Re-read pawn/lichess_data.py:118-142 and 361-416 plus grepped the whole tree for carve/holdout/partition: the only hit is the docstring at line 131. No row-level split exists anywhere. _scan_parquet's local-dir branch (lines 134-142) globs `<split>-*.parquet` and, when absent, falls back to ALL `*.parquet` identically for split='train' and split='validation'. The cache key includes `split` (lines 82-110), so train and val get distinct SHA dirs, but both scan the same files with the same filters, producing identical games (train uses max_games, val uses val_games -> overlapping head() prefixes). slice_batch (trainer.py:93) then samples val from this identical pool, so val loss echoes train. CONFIRMED, but scope is narrower than the title implies: it only bites for LOCAL single-file/undifferentiated-*.parquet sources. The default HF source thomas-schweich/pawn-lichess-full and any dir with train-*/validation-* shards have a real held-out validation split (extraction writes train/validation/test per scripts/extract_lichess_parquet.py and commit 3ac228b 'full holdout extraction'), so those do NOT leak. High is still defensible because when it does happen it is silent (no error, no warning, train==val), and CLAUDE.md actively advertises `--pgn-val-split ""` as a safe carve mode that does not exist.

title: Edge-case diagnostic masks predictions against the wrong ply (off-by-one)
description: The per-bit accuracy core aligns the model's prediction at sequence position t with the edge-case bit at ply t, but those describe two different moves. targets are built as targets[:, :-1] = tokens[:, 1:], so correct[:, t] measures whether the model correctly predicted move t+1. The engine's per-ply bits (per_ply[b, t]) are computed from the position BEFORE move t is applied (edgestats.rs: ply_bits[t] = compute_ply_bits(pos, ...) then state.make_move(token)), i.e. bits[:, t] is the edge condition for the move whose correct answer is move t. So `correct & mask` pairs 'predicted move t+1' with 'edge condition for move t'. The correctly-aligned pairing is correct[:, t-1] with bits[:, t] (equivalently, shift bits right by one along the ply axis before masking). Every per-label accuracy (in_check / double_check / pin_restricts / ep_available / castle_legal_* / checkmate / stalemate) is therefore computed on positions one ply away from the labelled condition. Affects both compute_edge_case_accuracy and the quota path.
evidence:
targets[:, :-1] = tokens[:, 1:]  # targets[t]=move t+1
...
pred = np.asarray(jnp.argmax(logits[..., :NUM_ACTIONS], axis=-1))  # pred[t] = predicted move t+1
correct = (pred_all == targets) & attn
...
mask = (bits & mask_value).astype(bool)   # bits[t] = board BEFORE move t
n_correct = int((correct & mask).sum())   # correct[t] vs bits[t]  -> off by one
suggestion: Align prediction-correctness with the labelled ply: either shift `bits` right by one along the ply axis (bits_shifted[:, 1:] = bits[:, :-1]) before masking, or mask `correct[:, :-1]` against `bits[:, 1:]`. Add a unit test that constructs a tiny game with a known in_check ply and asserts the diagnostic counts the prediction made AT that ply, not the following one.
verify_note: Verified against the engine source (engine/src/edgestats.rs:107-149,555-594). The module docstring and compute_ply_bits both state ply_bits[t] describes the board BEFORE the move at ply t is played; move_ids[t] is the move played from that position (state.make_move(token) at line 639 follows ply_bits[t]=bits at line 594). In _compute_per_bit_accuracy (diagnostics.py:141-153): targets[:, :-1]=tokens[:, 1:] so targets[t]=move_{t+1}; pred[t] is the model's prediction at position t = move_{t+1}; correct[t] therefore scores prediction of move_{t+1}. Masking correct[t] against bits[t] pairs 'predicted move t+1' with 'edge condition for the position that produced move t' — off by one. v1 (git show main:pawn/eval_suite/diagnostics.py:261-300) confirms intent: for a position labeled at ply t it builds prompt [m_0..m_{t-1}] and reads the logit at pred_pos=n_moves-1=t-1, i.e. it scores the prediction made AT the labeled ply. The correct v2 pairing is correct[:, :-1] vs bits[:, 1:] (equivalently shift bits right by one), exactly as the finder suggests. Affects every label in EDGE_CASE_LABELS via the shared core, so both compute_edge_case_accuracy and the quota path are wrong. As a side effect terminal labels (checkmate/stalemate at bits[length]) are scored against correct[length] whose target is PAD, compounding the misalignment. High severity is justified: this is the headline 'guaranteed-coverage' diagnostic and every per-label accuracy is computed one ply off.

title: Probe eval feeds synthetic Gaussian noise — the checkpoint's hidden states are never probed
description: eval_probes_jax.py loads the model only to read d_model, then fits the probe on rng.standard_normal hidden states with rng.integers random labels. The model never produces hidden states; the reported probe_accuracy is just a linear classifier fit to pure noise (expected ~1/n_classes), carrying no information about the checkpoint. This is wired into the batch orchestrator (run_evals_backbone.py invokes it per checkpoint and stores results['probes']), so the published eval bundle contains a meaningless number presented as a representation-quality probe. v1 (git show main:pawn/eval_suite/probes.py) extracted real chess features (piece_type, side_to_move, is_check, castling_rights, ep_square, material_count, legal_move_count, halfmove_clock, game_phase) from engine board states and probed per-layer hidden activations — that capability is silently lost. The fit_probe primitive itself is fine; there is no caller that extracts real frozen hidden states from PAWNModel and labels from engine.extract_board_states.
evidence:
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
hidden = jnp.asarray(rng.standard_normal((args.n_samples, d)).astype("float32"))
labels = jnp.asarray(rng.integers(0, args.n_classes, size=args.n_samples).astype("int32"))
cfg = ProbeConfig(n_classes=args.n_classes, n_epochs=args.n_epochs)
result = fit_probe(hidden, labels, cfg)   # model never used to produce `hidden`
suggestion: Wire a real hidden-state extraction path: run the frozen PAWNModel forward on engine-generated games, collect per-layer hidden states (model already supports a forward returning activations or this can be added), pair with labels from engine.extract_board_states (piece_type/is_check/etc.), and probe those. Until then the probe JSON should not be emitted as a real metric.
verify_note: Verified eval_probes_jax.py:29-39: model is loaded only to read d=model.cfg.d_model; hidden is rng.standard_normal((n_samples,d)) and labels are rng.integers(0,n_classes) — pure noise, model never produces hidden states. fit_probe on noise yields ~1/n_classes regardless of checkpoint. run_evals_backbone.py:42-50 confirms the orchestrator invokes this per checkpoint and stores results['probes'] alongside real accuracy/generation/lichess metrics, so a meaningless number is published as a representation-quality probe. The only fit_probe caller in non-test code is this script (grep confirms; the other hits are probes.py itself and test_jax_eval.py). engine.extract_board_states exists (engine/src/extract.rs, used by eval_suite/corpus.py) and v1 (git show main:pawn/eval_suite/probes.py) had a full real pipeline (piece_type/is_check/etc. features via extract_board_states, per-layer hidden-state extraction, train/val split, held-out eval) — that capability is silently lost in v2. The in-code comment claiming the 'realistic per-layer hidden-state extraction lives in S15 comprehensive tests' is misleading: that test (test_fit_probe_converges_on_separable_data) is a separability sanity check, not a real probe. Confirmed high.

title: schedule_health.json exit artifact silently dropped in v2 despite being documented as live
description: v1 wrote schedule_health.json next to metrics.jsonl at every trainer exit (pretrain + adapter), recording {planned_total_steps, actual_total_steps, completion_ratio, lr_peak, actual_final_lr, reason_for_stop}. It served two concrete functions: (1) the lab runner read it to detect schedule_complete vs early-exit, and (2) the trainer printed a red banner on the structural-bug signal actual!=planned AND reason==completed. v2 writes it nowhere. The FOCUS for this subsystem explicitly lists it, and the project's own CLAUDE.md still lists it under 'Key Patterns & Gotchas' as a current behavior, so this is a silently-lost capability, not an intentional drop. The trainer's post-loop block (lines 495-514) does producer.close, drain, logger.close, return 0 with no health write.
evidence: grep across the whole repo: `schedule_health` / `reason_for_stop` / `actual_total_steps` appear in NO .py file under pawn/ or scripts/. v1 (main) has pawn/adapter_training.py:705 `def write_schedule_health(...)` called at adapter_training.py:2139 and a structural-bug red banner at :753-761. v2 train_jax.py exit path: `producer.close(); ... drain_push_queue(...); push_tracker.shutdown(...); logger.close(); return 0` — no health artifact.
suggestion: Either implement a write_schedule_health equivalent (the trainer already tracks total_steps, next_step, schedule, schedule(0..) for lr_peak/actual_final_lr, and the break-reason is known: completed vs sigterm vs loader-exhausted) and emit it from both train_jax.py and train_jax_adapter.py exit paths, or, if the artifact is intentionally retired, remove it from CLAUDE.md's Key Patterns section so the documented contract matches the code.
verify_note: Verified by grep: `schedule_health`, `reason_for_stop`, `actual_total_steps` appear in ZERO .py files under pawn/ or scripts/ on HEAD. On main, `pawn/adapter_training.py:705 def write_schedule_health(...)` is called at :2139 (adapter exit) AND `pawn/trainer.py:1283-1285` imports+calls it (pretrain exit), with the structural-bug red banner at adapter_training.py:751-761 (actual!=planned AND reason in completed/step_limit). On main the artifact was read downstream by `pawn/lab/runner.py` and `pawn/lab/server.py`; on HEAD `pawn/lab/` has zero references to it. CLAUDE.md:436 still lists `schedule_health.json` under 'Key Patterns & Gotchas' as current behavior ('is written at trainer exit. Records {planned_total_steps, actual_total_steps, ...}'). train_jax.py:495-514 exit path is producer.close / drain / shutdown / logger.close / return 0 with no health write; train_jax_adapter.py:654-659 is the same. title: Sweep suggesters emit CLI flags the adapter entry point doesn't accept — bottleneck/sparse/all-rosa sweeps always fail
description: AdapterObjective builds the trial command via `_params_to_argv(params)`, turning each suggested param key into a kebab-case CLI flag. But several suggesters emit keys that scripts/train_jax_adapter.py's argparse does NOT register: suggest_bottleneck emits `bottleneck_n_hidden` -> `--bottleneck-n-hidden`; suggest_sparse emits `sparse_targets` -> `--sparse-targets`; suggest_rosa emits `rosa_warmup_steps`/`mask_samples`/`grad_alpha` -> `--rosa-warmup-steps`/`--mask-samples`/`--grad-alpha`; suggest_rosa_ratio emits `bottleneck_ratio` -> `--bottleneck-ratio`. These exist as AdapterConfig fields but have no CLI flag, so argparse exits with code 2; AdapterObjective then raises optuna.TrialPruned for every trial. Net effect: bottleneck, sparse, rosa, rosa-retro-sparse, rosa-retro-bottleneck, and rosa-ratio sweeps prune 100% of trials and study.best_value raises. Only lora/film/hybrid/unfreeze/specialized_clm sweep cleanly.
evidence: suggest_rosa returns {... 'rosa_warmup_steps': trial.suggest_int(...), 'mask_samples': trial.suggest_int(...), 'grad_alpha': trial.suggest_categorical('grad_alpha', [1, 2]), ...}; `_params_to_argv` -> ['--rosa-warmup-steps','...','--mask-samples','...','--grad-alpha','...']. grep of train_jax_adapter.py add_argument shows no --rosa-warmup-steps/--mask-samples/--grad-alpha/--sparse-targets/--bottleneck-n-hidden/--bottleneck-ratio. result.returncode != 0 -> raise optuna.TrialPruned.
suggestion: Either add the missing CLI flags to scripts/train_jax_adapter.py (--bottleneck-n-hidden, --sparse-targets, --sparse-ffn, --lora-ffn, --rosa-warmup-steps, --mask-samples, --grad-alpha) and a real handler for rosa-ratio, OR have AdapterObjective serialize the suggested params to a temp JSON and pass `--config <tmp>` instead of individual flags (the config path round-trips through pydantic and accepts every field). Add an integration test that actually invokes the adapter argparse with each suggester's emitted argv.
verify_note: Verified against scripts/train_jax_adapter.py:_parse_args (lines 180-231). Registered flags do NOT include --bottleneck-n-hidden, --sparse-targets, --rosa-warmup-steps, --mask-samples, --grad-alpha, or --bottleneck-ratio. The suggesters emit exactly these keys: suggest_bottleneck (sweep.py:67 'bottleneck_n_hidden'), suggest_sparse (sweep.py:86 'sparse_targets'), suggest_rosa (sweep.py:98-100 'rosa_warmup_steps'/'mask_samples'/'grad_alpha'), suggest_rosa_ratio (sweep.py:120 'bottleneck_ratio'). _params_to_argv (sweep.py:181-196) kebab-cases each, argparse exits code 2 on the unknown flag, and AdapterObjective (sweep.py:271-274) converts any non-zero returncode into optuna.TrialPruned. So bottleneck/sparse/rosa/rosa-retro-sparse/rosa-retro-bottleneck/rosa-ratio sweeps prune 100% of trials and study.best_value raises. lora/film/hybrid/unfreeze/specialized_clm emit only registered keys (lora_rank, lora_targets, use_output_film, no_adapt_attn, density, bottleneck_dim, unfreeze via n_layers_unfrozen->unfreeze_layers, d_model/n_layers/n_heads/d_ff, lr) and sweep cleanly. The test (tests/test_jax_sweep_lab_wandb.py) only checks dict membership and _params_to_argv kebab-casing, never that the argv is accepted by _parse_args, so the gap is uncaught. Note grad_alpha->--grad-alpha would also be a non-registered flag regardless of value. Real high-severity correctness defect: documented sweep strategies are entirely non-functional.

title: rosa-ratio is a selectable sweep strategy but is not a valid adapter --strategy
description: scripts/sweep.py restricts --strategy to choices=list(STRATEGY_SUGGESTERS), which includes 'rosa-ratio'. AdapterObjective then spawns `python scripts/train_jax_adapter.py --strategy rosa-ratio ...`. The adapter script's --strategy has no choices restriction, so argparse accepts it, but main() rejects it via `if cfg.strategy not in STRATEGIES: return 2` because STRATEGIES only has rosa/rosa-retro-sparse/rosa-retro-bottleneck. Every rosa-ratio trial therefore returns code 2 and is pruned.
evidence: STRATEGY_SUGGESTERS has key 'rosa-ratio' (pawn/sweep.py:170); STRATEGIES (pawn/adapter_trainer.py:105-144) has no 'rosa-ratio'. scripts/train_jax_adapter.py:291 `if cfg.strategy not in STRATEGIES: print(... unknown strategy ...); return 2`.
suggestion: Map rosa-ratio onto a real strategy: have suggest_rosa_ratio set strategy='rosa' in the trial command (it already sets rosa_mode='rosa') and pass bottleneck_ratio via a flag/config the rosa path consumes, or drop rosa-ratio from STRATEGY_SUGGESTERS until the bottleneck/sparse split knob is wired through AdapterConfig + RoSA init.
verify_note: scripts/sweep.py:17 restricts --strategy to choices=list(STRATEGY_SUGGESTERS), which includes 'rosa-ratio' (pawn/sweep.py:170). AdapterObjective spawns train_jax_adapter.py --strategy rosa-ratio. The adapter --strategy is required=False with no choices (train_jax_adapter.py:183), so argparse accepts it, but main() at line 291 'if cfg.strategy not in STRATEGIES: ... return 2' rejects it because STRATEGIES (adapter_trainer.py:105-147) has no 'rosa-ratio' key. Returns 2 -> TrialPruned. Even if strategy were mapped, --bottleneck-ratio is unregistered (overlaps the prior finding), so argparse would fail first. title: Pallas flash path silently discards attention_mask; correctness depends on an undocumented right-padding invariant that the type signature does not enforce
description: `_pallas_attn` does `del attention_mask` and calls `mha(..., segment_ids=None, causal=True)`. The docstring (lines 296-309) and the call-site comment (lines 735-739) BOTH claim PAD masking 'comes from attention_mask via segment_ids', but the code passes `segment_ids=None` — the two comments directly contradict the code. Correctness is actually salvaged by a different invariant: the Rust corpus emits strictly right-padded sequences (corpus.py:232-247 fills with PAD then overwrites a left-aligned prefix) and the loss masks PAD positions (trainer.py:217-221), so causal attention never lets a real query see a PAD key and PAD-query outputs are dropped from the loss. The flag is only ever set by trainers on right-padded batches, and generation uses the explicit-mask plain path, so it is not currently mis-fired. But nothing in the signature prevents a future caller from passing `use_flash=True` with a genuinely interior-padded or bidirectional mask and getting silently wrong attention with no error.
evidence: `del attention_mask  # see docstring — causal+right-pad makes this redundant` then `out_bthd = _pl_mha(q_bthd, k_bthd, v_bthd, segment_ids=None, sm_scale=float(inv_scale), causal=True)`. Contradicting comment at call site: `PAD-masking comes from attention_mask via segment_ids inside _pallas_attn`.
suggestion: Either derive `segment_ids` from `attention_mask` when a non-trivial (non-right-padded) mask is supplied, or assert/`eqx.error_if` that the mask is strictly right-padded (monotone non-increasing along T) when `use_flash=True`. At minimum fix the two comments that claim segment_ids are used so the code and docs agree.
verify_note: Verified directly. _pallas_attn (model.py:311) does `del attention_mask` and passes `segment_ids=None` (line 323), while BOTH the function docstring (296-309, which actually admits the drop is deliberate) and the call-site comment (737-739: 'PAD-masking comes from attention_mask via segment_ids inside _pallas_attn') describe segment_ids being used. The call-site comment directly contradicts the code. Correctness on current paths is genuinely salvaged: corpus.py:232-247 builds strictly right-padded sequences (np.full(PAD) then left-aligned overwrite, optional real outcome token at pos 0), causal attention prevents real queries from seeing PAD keys, and PAD-query outputs are dropped by the loss mask. The flash flag is set only by trainers on right-padded batches; generation uses the explicit-mask plain path (forward_with_cache is plain-attention-only per docstring 889-891). So no live mis-fire. The latent footgun is real: the type signature accepts an arbitrary Int[B,T] mask, and a future caller passing use_flash=True with an interior-padded or bidirectional mask gets silently wrong attention with no error. Medium is defensible given the silent-wrong-result failure mode for a plausible future caller, though one could argue low since it is purely latent.

title: Gradient accumulation (C.4) implemented and tested in make_train_step but unreachable from the production trainer
description: make_train_step fully implements an accumulation_steps>1 path (lax.scan over a leading microbatch axis, per-micro key fold, sum-then-scale grads). However scripts/train_jax.py:259-269 raises NotImplementedError whenever cfg.accumulation_steps != 1 because the bucketed prefetcher only emits (K,B,T) batches, never the (K,N,B,T) the accumulation path needs. So the C.4 win advertised in the docstring (effective batch 128 at B=64's per-step cost) cannot be obtained through the supported entry point — the entire accumulation branch is dead code in production, kept alive only by unit tests. This is a silent capability gap: a user setting accumulation_steps in a JSON config gets a hard crash, not the documented behavior.
evidence: trainer.py docstring claims the C.4 win; the body at 822-858 builds zero_grads, scans _acc_body over (micro_indices, batch), sums and scales. But train_jax.py:259: `if cfg.accumulation_steps != 1:` ... `raise NotImplementedError(... 'the prefetcher needs to produce (K, N, B, T)-shaped batches.')`. grep shows no caller passes accumulation_steps>1 except tests.
suggestion: Either wire the bucketed prefetcher to emit (K,N,B,T) batches so accumulation_steps>1 actually runs, or move/document the accumulation path as a benchmark-only feature. As-is the trainer docstring overstates a capability the only production caller refuses to use.
verify_note: Verified. trainer.py:760-858 fully implements the accumulation_steps>1 path: lax.scan over micro_indices with per-micro key fold (840-844), sum-then-scale (856-858). But train_jax.py:259 `if cfg.accumulation_steps != 1:` raises NotImplementedError (264-265) with the message that the prefetcher needs (K,N,B,T) batches. The only production caller hard-crashes on accumulation_steps != 1; run_config.py:324 exposes accumulation_steps as a configurable int field defaulting to 1, so a user setting it in JSON gets a crash, not the documented C.4 behavior. The accumulation branch is reachable only from unit tests. Medium is right: it's a documented-but-unreachable capability and a config field that crashes, but it fails loudly (NotImplementedError) rather than silently corrupting results, so not high.

title: epochs / steps_per_epoch / data_seed are validated but never consumed by the adapter trainer
description: AdapterConfig and SpecializedCLMConfig declare epochs, val_every, steps_per_epoch, and data_seed, and run validators on them (epochs>0, val_every>0, steps_per_epoch>0-or-'all', steps_per_epoch XOR max_games). CLAUDE.md states 'steps_per_epoch is canonical for adapters'. But scripts/train_jax_adapter.py drives its loop purely from cfg.total_steps via _run_steps(... range(n_steps)); it reads neither epochs, nor steps_per_epoch, nor data_seed (grep in the script finds no reads), and hardcodes batch-sampling RNG as np.random.default_rng(0)/default_rng(1) (lines 538-539). So the documented epoch-based cadence model is not wired, and runs cannot vary their data-sampling seed. These fields give a false sense of control and the validators guard inputs that have no effect.
evidence: run_config.py:446 `epochs: int = 50`, :455 `steps_per_epoch: ... = None`, :456 `data_seed: int | None = None`; train_jax_adapter.py:538-539 `rng = np.random.default_rng(0); val_rng = np.random.default_rng(1)`; `grep -n 'data_seed|steps_per_epoch|epochs' scripts/train_jax_adapter.py` returns no consuming reads.
suggestion: Either wire steps_per_epoch/epochs into the adapter loop's step budget and pass data_seed into the np.random.default_rng(...) calls, or remove the dead fields/validators and update CLAUDE.md to reflect that adapter cadence is total_steps-driven.
verify_note: Confirmed by code and by exhaustive grep. scripts/train_jax_adapter.py drives _run_steps purely off cfg.total_steps (range(n_steps), :559) and hardcodes np.random.default_rng(0)/default_rng(1) (:538-539). A repo-wide grep for data_seed/steps_per_epoch/.epochs/val_every outside run_config.py returns NOTHING in pawn/ or scripts/ (dashboard/model-card readers only display config values). So epochs, steps_per_epoch (incl. the 'all' resolution CLAUDE.md calls canonical), and data_seed are validated-but-unconsumed; runs cannot vary data-sampling seed and the documented epoch cadence is not wired. Real architecture/doc divergence. Medium is appropriate.

title: mate_boost ablation knob is never threaded into corpus generation
description: mate_boost is declared as an ablation field. The engine supports it (scripts/benchmark.py passes mate_boost=1.0 to engine.generate_random_games), but generate_corpus (pawn/corpus.py:310) does not even accept a mate_boost parameter, and train_jax.py never reads cfg.mate_boost. So the documented mate_boost ablation has no effect on any training run — it is silently inert.
evidence: run_config.py:118-119 `mate_boost: float = 0.0`; `grep -rn mate_boost pawn/ scripts/` shows it only in run_config.py, benchmark.py, and bucket_search.py — never in corpus.py/train_jax.py/trainer.py; corpus.py:310-316 generate_corpus signature has no mate_boost param.
suggestion: Either add a mate_boost passthrough to generate_corpus / engine.generate_random_games in the pretrain path, or drop the field if the ablation is out of scope for v2.
verify_note: Confirmed. grep shows mate_boost only in run_config.py:119, scripts/benchmark.py, and scripts/bench/bucket_search.py — never in corpus.py, trainer.py, or train_jax.py. generate_corpus's signature (corpus.py:309-316) has no mate_boost parameter, so even if train_jax read cfg.mate_boost there is no passthrough to engine.generate_random_games in the production pretrain path. The documented ablation knob is silently inert. The finder mislabels generate_corpus as not accepting prepend_outcome in the evidence sentence (it does accept prepend_outcome; it does NOT accept mate_boost) — the conclusion is correct, the cross-reference is just sloppy. Medium fair for a silently-inert ablation field.

title: FiLM output_gamma/output_beta sized to d_model, not vocab_size — output modulation applies to the wrong tensor
description: Separable from the core FiLM-semantics bug but worth isolating: the optional output FiLM in v1 modulated logits with parameters of shape vocab_size (FiLMLayer(cfg.vocab_size)). v2 declares output_gamma/output_beta as Float[Array, 'd'] (d_model) and folds them into final_norm_w. Even if the per-layer FiLM were fixed, the output head would still be modulating the final-norm weight per-d_model-channel rather than the per-vocab-class logits, so the output-FiLM capability is effectively lost/relocated. test_jax_adapters.py:657-668 asserts (d_model,) as 'v1 parity', which is incorrect.
evidence: output_gamma: Float[Array, "d"] | None ... new_final_norm_w = backbone.final_norm_w * adapter.output_gamma; new_final_norm_w = new_final_norm_w + adapter.output_beta
suggestion: If output FiLM is intended, size it to vocab_size and apply it to logits (needs a logits-stage hook or wrapper). Fix the test comment that claims (d_model,) is v1 parity.
verify_note: Re-read film.py:46-67,117-123 and v1. output_gamma/output_beta are declared Float[Array,'d'] (d_model), init'd ones/zeros at (d,), and folded into final_norm_w via final_norm_w*output_gamma + output_beta (lines 117-123). v1 used FiLMLayer(cfg.vocab_size) applied to logits in project_head. So even ignoring the per-layer bug, the 'output FiLM' modulates the final-norm weight per d_model channel rather than the per-vocab-class logits -- wrong tensor and wrong axis; the v1 output-FiLM capability is lost/relocated. test_jax_adapters.py:654-668 asserts output_gamma.shape==(d_model,) labeled 'v1 parity', which is incorrect (v1 was vocab_size). Confirmed; medium is right since it's a subset/sibling of film-not-film and on its own affects only the optional output head.

title: training_state.json never stores scheduler/RNG despite docs claiming it does; RNG is silently reset to key(0) on resume
description: The checkpoint docstring (line 19) and CLAUDE.md both state training_state.json carries {"step", "scheduler", "rng"}. The only writer call sites pass training_state={"step": int(state.step)} (scripts/train_jax.py:426, scripts/train_jax_adapter.py:515,533) — no scheduler, no rng. v1 (git show main:pawn/checkpoint.py) genuinely base64-persisted torch+cuda RNG state and scheduler.state_dict; v2 dropped both. load_resume_state always overwrites the key with a caller-supplied jax.random.key(0) (pawn/lifecycle.py:447, scripts/train_jax.py:231, scripts/train_jax_adapter.py:413,623), so any saved RNG would be ignored anyway. The practical correctness impact is currently nil because state.key is a fixed constant in every code path and per-step randomness is re-derived deterministically as jax.random.fold_in(state.key, state.step) (pawn/trainer.py:813) with state.key carried unchanged (pawn/trainer.py:874) — resume at step N reproduces the same fold_in draw the original run had at step N. The scheduler is likewise reconstructable from the restored Optax count. The defect is doc/contract drift that misrepresents the resume guarantee: an operator reading the canonical orientation doc believes RNG/scheduler are durably round-tripped when they are not, and any future change that splits/advances state.key in the loop would silently break exact resume reproducibility with no checkpoint field to recover from.
evidence: checkpoint.py:19 `- ``training_state.json`` (optional) — ``{"step", "scheduler", "rng"}``` vs scripts/train_jax.py:426 `training_state={"step": int(state.step)},`; lifecycle.py:447 `key=key,` where key is `jax.random.key(0)` from train_jax.py:231.
suggestion: Either (a) actually persist rng (jax.random.key_data(state.key), base64) + read it back in load_resume_state so the documented contract holds, or (b) correct the docstring and CLAUDE.md to state only {"step"} is stored and that per-step randomness is fold_in-derived from a fixed key so resume is reproducible without an RNG field. If keeping (b), add an assertion/comment at the train_step that state.key must remain a loop-invariant constant, since the resume-reproducibility argument depends on it.
verify_note: Verified directly. checkpoint.py:19 docstring claims training_state.json carries {"step","scheduler","rng"}, and CLAUDE.md repeats it. All three writer sites pass only {"step": int(state.step)} (train_jax.py:426, train_jax_adapter.py:515,533). load_resume_state (lifecycle.py:443-448) always sets key=<caller key>, and every caller passes a fixed jax.random.key(0) (train_jax.py:231, train_jax_adapter.py:415). The trainer step body keeps key=state.key unchanged (trainer.py:874) and re-derives per-step randomness as fold_in(state.key, state.step) (trainer.py:813), so resume reproducibility currently holds with the fixed key — the practical correctness impact is nil today. v1 (main:pawn/checkpoint.py:380-385,442-449) genuinely persisted scheduler_state_dict + base64 torch/cuda RNG and restored them; v2 dropped this. Per the review's v1-compat-drop rule this is not flagged as a parity regression, but the docstring/CLAUDE.md still advertise an RNG/scheduler round-trip that does not exist. Real doc/contract drift; medium is justified because the stale contract masks a latent reproducibility footgun if state.key is ever split/advanced in the loop. The finder's own analysis and suggestion (b) are sound.

title: `pgn_val_split=""` silently coerces to "validation" instead of carve-from-train
description: The carve-from-train opt-in documented as `--pgn-val-split ""` is consumed as `split=cfg.pgn_val_split or "validation"`. An empty string is falsy, so `"" or "validation"` evaluates to `"validation"` — the empty-string sentinel is discarded and the val load requests the validation split. Combined with the missing carve implementation, the documented escape hatch is doubly inert: the sentinel never reaches `load_lichess_corpus`, and even if it did there is no carve code path.
evidence: split=cfg.pgn_val_split or "validation"  # "" -> "validation"
suggestion: Distinguish `None`/unset from the explicit empty-string sentinel (`cfg.pgn_val_split if cfg.pgn_val_split is not None else "validation"`), and route the empty-string case into a real carve-from-train branch.
verify_note: Traced the full path. CLI default is None (train_jax_adapter.py:188); _build_config merges any non-None CLI value into the pydantic config (line 263 `if val is None: continue` — empty string is NOT None, so base['pgn_val_split']="" IS set and reaches cfg). Then at line 461 `split=cfg.pgn_val_split or "validation"` coerces "" -> "validation" because empty string is falsy. So the empty-string sentinel survives the merge but is then discarded by the `or`. Combined with the total absence of a carve code path (verdict above), the documented escape hatch is doubly inert exactly as the finding states. For HF/split-structured sources this is benign (you get the real validation split). For local single-file sources it routes into the leak above. Medium is appropriate; the fix (distinguish None from "") is correct.

title: fit_probe reports training-set accuracy (no held-out split)
description: fit_probe trains on (hidden_states, labels) for n_epochs, then computes final accuracy on the exact same hidden_states/labels it trained on. For a linear probe this is an in-sample (training) accuracy that overestimates generalization, especially when d is large relative to N (d_model 256-640 vs default n_samples 1024). A linear-probe representation metric should be evaluated on held-out data. There is no train/val partition anywhere in the function or its caller.
evidence:
for _ in range(cfg.n_epochs):
    idx = rng.permutation(n)
    ... params, state, _ = step(...)
...
logits = hidden_states @ w + b   # same array trained on
preds = jnp.argmax(logits, axis=-1)
acc = float((preds == labels).mean())
suggestion: Split inputs into train/eval folds (or accept separate eval arrays), fit on train, report accuracy on the held-out fold. This is also the natural place to compare layers without the in-sample inflation confounding the comparison.
verify_note: Verified probes.py:80-95: fit_probe trains on the full (hidden_states, labels) for n_epochs then computes logits = hidden_states @ w + b on the exact same arrays and reports that in-sample accuracy. No train/val partition in the function or any caller. For a linear probe with d_model 256-640 and default n_samples 1024 this materially overestimates generalization. fit_probe is a public reusable primitive (in __all__) and v1's probe pipeline explicitly used held-out evaluation (git show main:pawn/eval_suite/probes.py has _eval_in_batches on separate val_data), so this is a genuine design regression for any real use, independent of the synthetic-noise caller. Medium is appropriate.

title: Move-accuracy / per-phase eval ignores the checkpoint's prepend_outcome and bins by sequence index
description: eval_jax.py always builds the eval corpus with generate_corpus(..., prepend_outcome=False) (the default), never reading the training run config that the checkpoint stores (checkpoint.py persists the `run` block which carries prepend_outcome). compute_per_phase_accuracy then bins positions by raw sequence index t (opening t<20, midgame 20<=t<60, endgame t>=60). When prepend_outcome=False, t==ply so binning is correct; but if the model was trained with prepend_outcome=True, position 0 is an outcome token and every move is shifted right by one. Evaluating such a model with prepend_outcome=False creates a train/eval distribution mismatch (position 0 becomes a move, not the outcome token the model expects) AND the phase boundaries are off by one ply. The eval silently produces numbers under the wrong layout.
evidence: corpus = generate_corpus(\n    n_games=args.n_games, max_ply=args.max_ply, seq_len=args.seq_len, seed=0\n)   # prepend_outcome defaults False, never derived from checkpoint config
suggestion: Read prepend_outcome from the loaded checkpoint's run config and pass it through to generate_corpus; thread the same offset into PhaseBoundaries (bin by ply = t - outcome_offset) so phase boundaries stay aligned regardless of prefix mode.
verify_note: Verified prepend_outcome lives only in BaseRunConfig (run_config.py:122), not ModelConfig (config.py only mentions it in a comment), so the loaded PAWNModel does not self-describe it. eval_jax.py:31-33 calls generate_corpus(...) with no prepend_outcome -> default False (corpus.py:193), and load_model (checkpoint.py:406) returns only the model, never the persisted 'run' block (checkpoint.py:318-319 stores run config but eval doesn't read it). compute_per_phase_accuracy bins by raw sequence index t (eval.py:129-132). For an outcome-prefix-trained checkpoint this both creates a layout mismatch (position 0 is a move, not the outcome token the model saw in training) and shifts phase boundaries by one ply, producing silently-wrong numbers. Real and silent, but bounded: only affects prepend_outcome=True checkpoints and the supernet default is False. Medium confirmed. Note: the same latent bug extends to scripts/eval_vs_stockfish.py, which calls load_lichess_corpus (lichess_data.py:370 prepend_outcome default False) without threading the checkpoint's prepend_outcome — same root cause in the lichess eval path.

title: eval_vs_stockfish.py also ignores prepend_outcome when building lichess corpora
description: Parallel to the eval_jax.py prepend_outcome finding: eval_vs_stockfish.py calls load_lichess_corpus(...) without passing prepend_outcome, which defaults to False (pawn/lichess_data.py:370). For an outcome-prefix-trained checkpoint the Elo-stratified accuracy is computed on the wrong sequence layout (position 0 becomes a move rather than the outcome token the model was trained to see at slot 0), silently producing biased per-bin accuracy. This is wired into run_evals_backbone.py (stores results['lichess']). Same root cause as eval-ignores-prepend-outcome-config but in the lichess eval path, which the original finding (scoped to eval_jax.py) did not call out. Fix: read prepend_outcome from the checkpoint's persisted run config and thread it through load_lichess_corpus.
evidence: (surfaced by skeptic pass)
verify_note: Found by adversarial skeptic.

title: New PAD-init regression test is tautological and cannot catch a regression in the actual code paths
description: test_token_buffer_pad_init_contract constructs its own fresh `vec![vocab::PAD_TOKEN as i16; n * max_ply]` and asserts every element equals PAD_TOKEN. That only re-verifies the semantics of Rust's `vec!` macro — it never invokes uci_to_tokens, parse_pgn_enriched, parse_pgn_lichess, or parse_pgn_sampled. If someone reverted any of those four init sites back to `vec![0i16; ...]`, this test would still pass. The docstring itself concedes it operates 'at the vec-init level' rather than exercising the real flow, so the regression guard the comment claims to provide does not exist.
evidence: Lines 1753-1759 build a local buffer and assert on it: `let buf = vec![vocab::PAD_TOKEN as i16; n * max_ply]; for v in &buf { assert_eq!(*v, vocab::PAD_TOKEN as i16, ...) }`. No call to any of the four exported functions appears in the test.
suggestion: Replace with a test that calls one of the real exported paths (e.g. drive uci_to_tokens/parse_pgn_* with a short game and a large max_ply/seq_len, then assert the trailing slots beyond game_length equal PAD_TOKEN and not 0). That is the only way to lock the four init sites against regression.
verify_note: Lines 1749-1765: test_token_buffer_pad_init_contract constructs a fresh local `vec![vocab::PAD_TOKEN as i16; n*max_ply]` and asserts each element equals PAD_TOKEN, plus two decompose_token assertions on vocab semantics. It never calls uci_to_tokens, parse_pgn_enriched, parse_pgn_lichess, or parse_pgn_sampled. Reverting any of the four real init sites to vec![0i16] would leave this test green — it only re-verifies Rust's vec! macro and vocab decompose behavior, not the production code paths. The docstring's own 'at the vec-init level' wording concedes it does not exercise the real flow. Medium maintainability severity is justified: it gives false regression-protection confidence.

title: --wandb is a silent no-op; pawn.wandb_utils is never called by any v2 entry point

So --wandb is accepted and silently does nothing. The module docstring's claim 'Every v2 training entry point funnels through init_wandb / log_metrics / finish_wandb' is false. title: attn_hook/ffn_hook supplied with hook_data=None calls the hook with hook_slice=None instead of skipping it
description: `has_hooks` requires BOTH a hook callable AND non-None `hook_data`. When `has_hooks` is False the scan input is just `self.layers`, so `hook_slice=None` in the body. But the per-sublayer guards only check `if attn_hook is not None:` / `if ffn_hook is not None:` — they do NOT re-check `has_hooks`. So a caller that passes `attn_hook=fn, hook_data=None` will invoke `fn(h, None)`, almost certainly crashing inside the adapter (which indexes per-layer slices) or, worse, silently no-op'ing if the hook tolerates None. The current sole caller (BottleneckEffective) always pairs hooks with a non-None `hook_data`, so this is latent, not live.
evidence: `has_hooks = (attn_hook is not None or ffn_hook is not None) and hook_data is not None` ... `if attn_hook is not None: h = attn_hook(h, hook_slice)` — the second condition does not include `has_hooks`, so hook_slice can be None.
suggestion: Gate the hook invocations on `has_hooks` (e.g. `if attn_hook is not None and has_hooks`), or raise a ValueError at the top of `__call__`/`forward_with_cache` when a hook is provided without hook_data, so the inconsistent-args case fails loudly rather than passing None into the hook.
verify_note: Verified in both code paths. _run_layers: has_hooks = (attn_hook is not None or ffn_hook is not None) and hook_data is not None (690-692); when hook_data is None, has_hooks is False so the scan carries only self.layers and hook_slice=None (700-702), yet the invocation guards are `if attn_hook is not None` (780) and `if ffn_hook is not None` (811), which do NOT re-check has_hooks. forward_with_cache repeats the exact same pattern (929-931, 1036, 1059). So a caller supplying a hook callable with hook_data=None invokes hook(h, None). Confirmed latent: an adapter hook that indexes a per-layer slice from hook_slice will crash on None, or silently no-op if it tolerates None. No live caller hits this (the sole hook caller pairs callables with non-None hook_data). Low is correct: latent, not live, and tends to fail loudly rather than corrupt.

title: RoPE now applied in compute dtype (bf16) rather than fp32; deliberate but is a real numerical-policy change vs the rest of the precision recipe
description: `_apply_rope` downcasts the fp32 rope tables to `x.dtype` and does the rotation in `x.dtype`. Under bf16 compute this means Q/K rotation accumulates `x0*cos - x1*sin` in bf16, unlike RMSNorm and softmax which the module is otherwise careful to keep in fp32 (see _rmsnorm and the score upcast at line 770). The docstring argues this is below bf16 noise at T<=512, which is plausible for a unit-norm rotation, but it is an asymmetry in the precision policy: every other numerically-sensitive reduction upcasts, RoPE does not. Worth flagging because it is the kind of thing that silently shifts when someone later raises max_seq_len or changes rope_base. Not a defect under the current shapes.
evidence: `cos = rope_cos.astype(x.dtype)` / `sin = rope_sin.astype(x.dtype)` then `out0 = x0 * cos - x1 * sin` — all in x.dtype, with no fp32 intermediate, contrasted with `_rmsnorm` which upcasts to fp32.
suggestion: Keep as-is for perf but make the precision contract explicit in the precision-policy docstring (module header lists RMSNorm/RoPE in fp32 at lines 33-40, which now disagrees with the code) so the asymmetry is intentional-by-record, not drift.
verify_note: Verified. _apply_rope (271-278) downcasts the fp32 rope tables to x.dtype and does out0 = x0*cos - x1*sin entirely in x.dtype, with no fp32 intermediate — contrasting with _rmsnorm (upcasts to fp32) and the attention score path (770: scores.astype(jnp.float32) before softmax). So RoPE is the one numerically-sensitive op left in compute dtype. This is explicitly intentional and documented in _apply_rope's own docstring (251-258: the fp32 upcast was deliberately removed to avoid a (B,H,T,d) fp32 materialisation; Llama refs apply RoPE in compute dtype; rotation is unit-norm and below bf16 noise at T<=512). The substantive value of the finding is the documentation-asymmetry / future-drift risk (e.g. if max_seq_len or rope_base later increases), not a current defect. Low is correct.

title: Module-level docstring states 'RoPE applied in fp32' but the implementation applies it in compute dtype
description: The module header (line 40) says '**RoPE applied in fp32** to Q and K, then downcast — same reason.' The actual `_apply_rope` (lines 271-278) does the opposite: it downcasts the tables to `x.dtype` and rotates in compute dtype, and its own docstring (lines 247-269) explicitly explains why the fp32 upcast was REMOVED. The two docstrings within the same file contradict each other. A reader trusting the header will mis-model the bf16 numerics.
evidence: Header line 40: `**RoPE applied in fp32** to Q and K, then downcast`. Function lines 253-258: `Earlier versions upcast x to fp32 ... the explicit upcast cost a full (B, H, T, d_head) fp32 materialisation per Q + K call`.
suggestion: Update the module header bullet to match `_apply_rope`'s actual compute-dtype behaviour.
verify_note: Verified exactly. Module header line 40: '**RoPE applied in fp32** to Q and K, then downcast — same reason.' The implementation (_apply_rope, 271-278) downcasts the tables to x.dtype and rotates in compute dtype, and the function's own docstring (251-258) explains the fp32 upcast was removed. Genuine in-file contradiction that would mislead a reader modelling bf16 numerics. Documentation-only; low is correct.

title: _build_rope docstring also contradicts the implementation's compute-dtype RoPE
description: A third stale docstring the finder missed: _build_rope's docstring states 'The per-step RoPE application upcasts Q/K to fp32 before multiplying through, so storing the tables in fp32 is the canonical form' (lines 227-229). This is the opposite of what _apply_rope now does (downcasts tables to x.dtype, rotates in compute dtype, lines 271-278). So there are at least three in-file statements disagreeing with the actual RoPE precision behaviour: module header line 40, _build_rope lines 227-229, vs the corrected _apply_rope docstring at 251-258. Any fix to the precision-contract documentation should cover all three sites, not just the module header flagged in the existing findings.
